core_obligations: Set up the two colimits (proof lines 4281-4295): choosing an affine neighbourhood of s, the author writes both the strict henselization and the stalk as filtered colimits of the same kind of rings, over etale neighbourhoods of the geometric point.
Compare them (proof lines 4295-4309): the two colimits are indexed by the same filtering category with the same transition maps, so they are canonically identified, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Write the strict henselization as a colimit of etale algebras over an affine neighbourhood.
Write the stalk as a colimit over the same etale neighbourhoods.
Identify the two colimits, which are canonically the same.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the stalk of the structure sheaf on the small etale site with the strict henselization of the local ring, in the form of a canonical identification of the two filtered colimits over etale neighbourhoods (statement lines 4256-4279, whose slogan line is excluded from the counted spans as explained in the notes). The proof writes both objects as filtered colimits over etale neighbourhoods of the geometric point (proof lines 4281-4295) and identifies them because the index categories and transition maps coincide (proof lines 4295-4309). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two colimit descriptions. The claim is H2: one comparison of colimits.
